div.h2: 📦 1. Splunk Technology Add-on (TA) Architecture: Avoiding Package Bloat

div.style: background: rgba(14, 165, 233, 0.08); border-left: 4px solid #0284c7; padding: 14px 18px; border-radius: 0 6px 6px 0; margin-bottom: 16px;
div.b: Architectural Rule: Decoupling Telemetry Generation from Field Extraction
div.p: A common anti-pattern in network simulation is bundling dozens of third-party Splunk Technology Add-ons (e.g., Cisco, Palo Alto, Fortinet, Arista TAs) inside a single application. Doing so creates severe application bloat (expanding a 5MB app into several gigabytes), triggers Python library conflicts, and causes automatic rejection during Splunk Cloud AppInspect vetting.
NetSpout solves this cleanly:

ul.li: 100% Schema-Accurate Output: NetSpout formats raw syslogs, OpenConfig JSON-IETF, and SC4SNMP payloads to perfectly match what official vendor hardware emits.

Standard CIM Normalization: When official vendor TAs are installed on Search Heads or Indexers, they immediately recognize NetSpout sourcetypes and parse fields into CIM data models (Network Sessions, Network Traffic, Performance, Authentication).
Splunk Cloud & Enterprise Vetted: NetSpout contains zero bundled third-party binaries, zero unvetted dependencies, and complies 100% with Splunk AppInspect requirements.

div.p: NetSpout routes high-frequency OpenConfig YANG paths and SC4SNMP polling counters into the dedicated 500GB metric tier (cisco_mdt_metrics). Use | mstats for sub-second analytics:
Lists all unique metric channels and current average values:

pre.style: background: #0b0f19; padding: 10px; border-radius: 4px; color: #38bdf8; font-family: monospace; font-size: 11px; overflow-x: auto; margin: 0;

div.pre: | mstats avg(_value) WHERE index=cisco_mdt_metrics metric_name=* BY metric_name

div.p: Computes throughput rates across OpenConfig interface counters:

pre.style: background: #0b0f19; padding: 10px; border-radius: 4px; color: #10b981; font-family: monospace; font-size: 11px; overflow-x: auto; margin: 0;

div.pre: | mstats rate(interface.octets.in) AS in_bps, rate(interface.octets.out) AS out_bps WHERE index=cisco_mdt_metrics span=10s BY host, interface

div.p: Tracks link flaps generated during simulated fiber cuts:

pre.style: background: #0b0f19; padding: 10px; border-radius: 4px; color: #ef4444; font-family: monospace; font-size: 11px; overflow-x: auto; margin: 0;

div.pre: | mstats sum(carrier.transitions) AS flaps WHERE index=cisco_mdt_metrics span=30s BY host

div.p: Monitors hardware platform telemetry during resource saturation:

pre.style: background: #0b0f19; padding: 10px; border-radius: 4px; color: #f59e0b; font-family: monospace; font-size: 11px; overflow-x: auto; margin: 0;

div.pre: | mstats latest(platform.cpu.utilization) AS cpu, latest(platform.memory.utilization) AS mem WHERE index=cisco_mdt_metrics span=10s BY host

div.h4: BGP FSM State & Prefix Rib Counters
div.p: Audits BGP peering state (6=Established, 1=Idle) and route counts:

pre.style: background: #0b0f19; padding: 10px; border-radius: 4px; color: #a855f7; font-family: monospace; font-size: 11px; overflow-x: auto; margin: 0;

div.pre: | mstats latest(bgp.peer.state) AS fsm_state, latest(bgp.prefixes.received) AS pfx_rcv WHERE index=cisco_mdt_metrics BY host, peer

div.p: Analyzes 64-bit SNMP polling metrics streamed by the SC4SNMP engine:

pre.style: background: #0b0f19; padding: 10px; border-radius: 4px; color: #06b6d4; font-family: monospace; font-size: 11px; overflow-x: auto; margin: 0;

div.pre: | mstats rate(ifHCInOctets) AS rx_bps, rate(ifHCOutOctets) AS tx_bps WHERE index=cisco_mdt_metrics span=15s BY host, ifIndex

h2.style: color: #a855f7; font-size: 16px; margin-top: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px;

div.h2: 🔍 4. Production SPL Queries: Event Indexes (idx_network_ops, cisco_secure_fw)
div.p: Explore raw event telemetry, syslog alarms, SC4SNMP traps, and multi-device fault cascades:
Parses decoded SNMP traps with varbinds:

pre.style: background: #0b0f19; padding: 10px; border-radius: 4px; color: #ef4444; font-family: monospace; font-size: 11px; overflow-x: auto; margin: 0;

div.pre: index=idx_network_ops sourcetype="sc4snmp:event" snmp_trap_name=* | table _time, host, snmp_trap_name, snmp_trap_oid, severity, varbinds.ifDescr

div.p: Correlates interface carrier down with neighbor routing loss:

pre.style: background: #0b0f19; padding: 10px; border-radius: 4px; color: #f59e0b; font-family: monospace; font-size: 11px; overflow-x: auto; margin: 0;

div.pre: index=idx_network_ops (sourcetype="cisco:ios:syslog" OR sourcetype="juniper:syslog") ("%LINK-3-UPDOWN" OR "%BGP-5-ADJCHANGE" OR "%OSPF-5-ADJCHG") | stats count, values(message) by host

div.h4: Next-Gen Firewall Session Drops & SYN Floods
div.p: Identifies DDoS attack patterns and state table saturation:

pre.style: background: #0b0f19; padding: 10px; border-radius: 4px; color: #38bdf8; font-family: monospace; font-size: 11px; overflow-x: auto; margin: 0;

div.pre: index=idx_security_fw (sourcetype="pan:traffic" OR sourcetype="cisco:sfw:estreamer") action="drop" | timechart span=1m count by app

div.p: Monitors device health scores and client connectivity issues:

pre.style: background: #0b0f19; padding: 10px; border-radius: 4px; color: #10b981; font-family: monospace; font-size: 11px; overflow-x: auto; margin: 0;

div.pre: index=idx_network_ops sourcetype="cisco:catalyst:devicehealth" | spath path=healthScore output=score | stats avg(score) as avg_health, min(score) as min_health by host

div.h2: 🚀 5. Production Deployment: Splunk Cloud, Enterprise & Standalone Docker

ol.li: In Splunk Web, go to Apps > Manage Apps > Install app from file.
Upload the certified release package: netspout.spl.
Ensure HEC is enabled under Settings > Data Inputs > HTTP Event Collector.
The app automatically provisions the 500GB cisco_mdt_metrics index and event tiers.
